claims.claim: The page is scoped to DeepGEMM commit 891d57b, accurately identifies the project and its SM90/SM100 requirements, and distinguishes two representative local FP8 1D1D files from the full multi-kernel library.

evidence.observation: The README identifies the library, SM90/SM100 requirements, runtime-compiled design, and multiple dense/grouped/attention/MoE interfaces.
The two representative files are pinned to the same commit and carry matching SHA-256 values.

challenge.alternative: The commit link is only decorative and the local files come from a different revision or represent the whole repository.
challenge.check: Compare the frontmatter, README tree, provenance upstream SHA, and exact file hashes.
challenge.outcome: The revision matches across the page and manifest, hashes match, and the pinned tree visibly contains many other kernel/API files.

claims.claim: The DeepSeek-V3 1x128 activation and 128x128 weight scaling geometry, scoped outlier motivation, architecture-specific FP32 versus packed-UE8M0 representations, four-value packing, and pinned K-granularity statements are accurate.

evidence.observation: The paper specifies the two granularities and says smaller groups better accommodate outliers; it does not promise elimination of quantization error.
SM90 uses FP32 factors and SM100 uses packed UE8M0 with four values per torch.int.
The SM100 template fixes BLOCK_K to 128 and permits scale K granularities 32 or 128; the corresponding SM90 file fixes BLOCK_K to 128.

challenge.alternative: Both operands use 128x128 blocks and every architecture consumes FP32 scales.
challenge.check: Compare the paper's separate operand rules and the pinned README/kernel types.
challenge.outcome: Activation grouping is per row, while the SM100 representation and accepted granularities differ explicitly from SM90.

claims.claim: The H800 retained-bit description, Nc=128 K-element/four-WGMMA interval, four-step walkthrough, and verbatim six-line excerpt of the pinned SM90 accum/final_accum promotion path match the paper and source.

evidence.observation: The report states about 14 retained bits, promotion every 128 inner-dimension elements, equivalence to four WGMMAs, and FP32 CUDA-core accumulation.

evidence.locator: math warp-group loop from accum declarations through Promote with scales and store
evidence.observation: The code declares float accum/final_accum, loads FP32 A/B factors, issues and waits for WGMMA for one BLOCK_K=128 stage, scales into final_accum, and stages final values for store.

challenge.alternative: Nc=128 describes 128 output columns and the real accumulator is half precision as in the deleted sketch.
challenge.check: Trace the k_block loop and declared C++ types and compare Nc's definition in the paper.
challenge.outcome: The interval advances K, WGMMA output registers are declared float, and promotion targets a separate float array.

claims.claim: The SM100 walkthrough accurately describes the float/UE8M0 block-scaled instruction descriptor, TMA-to-shared and UTCCP-to-TMEM scale path, elected UMMA issue operands, TMEM accumulator lifecycle, absence of SM90 final_accum promotion, and precision qualification.

evidence.locator: TMA scale loads, make_instr_desc_block_scaled, UTCCP copies, mma_t::fma, tmem barriers, and epilogue
evidence.observation: Each stated data-movement, descriptor, issue, and lifecycle element appears in the pinned source. The template selects accumulator and scale types rather than asserting a universal tcgen05 precision mode.

challenge.alternative: Packed scales remain in general registers and are immediate MMA operands, while TMEM holds only output.
challenge.check: Follow smem_sfa/sfb through the UTCCP copy destinations and the final fma arguments.
challenge.outcome: The copies target dedicated TMEM scale columns and fma receives their TMEM addresses separately from the TMEM accumulator column.

claims.claim: The grouped-interface table and surrounding text correctly distinguish M-grouped contiguous, M-grouped masked, and K-grouped contiguous shapes, metadata, purposes, alignment, and pinned SM90-NT/SM100-TN K-grouped variants.

evidence.locator: Grouped GEMMs contiguous and masked sections
evidence.observation: The README gives the M-grouped fixed-axis/use-case rules, segment alignment, masked decode role, and separate K-axis weight-backward API.

The API checks establish each tensor shape and metadata type; contiguous supports M-length or group-count metadata forms, masked_m is an int valid-length vector, and K-grouped dispatches TN only to SM100 and NT only to SM90.

challenge.alternative: Masked mode uses a Boolean element mask and K-grouped is merely a third M-grouped storage layout.
challenge.check: Inspect masked_m dtype/shape and the K-grouped shape equations.
challenge.outcome: masked_m has one int per group, while K-grouped sums per-group K lengths and fixes the output's M/N.

claims.claim: The pinned JIT defaults to NVCC, optionally selects NVRTC through DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=1 with a performance caveat, keys the cache by kernel/compiler/flags/code, compiles and publishes misses, reuses hits, and makes no optimality guarantee.

evidence.observation: NVRTC is optional, defaults off, and may perform worse in some cases.
The code constructs the stated signature, returns cache hits, compiles/publishes misses atomically, and selects NVCC unless the environment opt-in is nonzero.

challenge.alternative: NVRTC is the mandatory/default JIT and every invocation recompiles the specialization.
challenge.check: Evaluate the compiler selection default and the early cache-hit return.
challenge.outcome: The default expression is zero, selecting NVCC, and a valid cached runtime returns before compilation.

claims.claim: The pinned FP8 interface supports NT only on SM90 and NT/TN/NN/TT on SM100, with public wrappers and SM100 operand-major parameters implementing the additional layouts.

evidence.locator: Interfaces notices and normal dense GEMMs
evidence.observation: The README states the exact architecture/layout support and naming convention.
The wrappers transpose relevant views and pass major modes; the SM90 path asserts K-major inputs.

challenge.alternative: The four SM100 names all demand physically NT inputs and do not alter descriptors.
challenge.check: Trace tensor-view transformations and kMajorA/kMajorB into the SM100 template.
challenge.outcome: Different wrappers transform A and/or B and the selected major values reach descriptor construction.

claims.claim: The only retained numeric performance statement is the pinned project's source-reported up-to 1550 TFLOPS on H800, explicitly qualified as lacking the former 4096-cubed shape, 90% utilization, and a complete reproducibility envelope.

evidence.observation: The README says up to 1550 TFLOPS on H800 and supplies none of the deleted shape/utilization conditions.
A nearby disclosed peak result uses M=4096, N=7168, K=16384, helping discriminate it from the page's former unsupported 4096-cubed attribution.

challenge.alternative: The up-to result proves the former 4096-cubed and 90% row by implication.
challenge.check: Search the pinned README and linked performance history for that condition tuple.
challenge.outcome: The README supplies neither field, and the available shape-scoped peak evidence names a different tuple; the page now says exactly that.

claims.claim: The practical boundaries accurately separate input preparation from GEMM, state project warnings and grouped/JIT constraints, and avoid claiming a universal fine-grained-scaling cost or decision rule.

evidence.observation: The project says transposition and FP8 casting are user-side operations and that its utility implementations may be slower than fusing them into prior kernels.
The paper describes the precision motivation and says the scale multiplication has minimal extra computational cost in its Hopper promotion strategy; it does not establish a universal cost ordering.

challenge.alternative: Every extra scale necessarily makes the end-to-end kernel slower than per-tensor scaling, so target/workload qualifications are evasive.
challenge.check: Separate arithmetic count from native instruction support, scale preparation/fusion, and the measured scope in the primary sources.
challenge.outcome: The sources establish architecture-dependent mechanisms and no controlled universal comparison; conditional wording is the strongest supported conclusion.
